name: Memphis Grizzlies
headline: The Grizzlies are 7-4 and outscoring teams by 6 a game, but they have lost four of their last six.
good: Memphis averages 117.9 points and allows 111.9, a net of +6.0, with a 115.2 offensive rating and 109.4 defensive rating.
Ty Jerome leads the way at 26.2 points a game on 62.5% true shooting, and he scored 27 in the win at Toronto that made Memphis 5-0 on the road.
Rookie Cameron Boozer is at 16.1 points, 9.9 rebounds and 5.5 assists, and had a triple-double against Portland.
The team shoots 38.9% from three and 85.3% at the line, and it started 6-0 before the recent slide.
bad: Memphis lost 134-135 to New Orleans, 103-107 to Indiana, 97-128 to Oklahoma City and 118-123 to Denver, four losses in its last six games.
Turnovers are a problem at 15.5 a game against 13.2 forced, and the team also trails opponents in steals (5.9 vs 7.7) and blocks (4.9 vs 7.3).
Boozer shoots only 50.7% true shooting on a 25% usage rate, and Jaylen Wells is at 12.0 points with just 2.7 rebounds.
fans: Early coverage has been enthusiastic about Boozer and Jerome, with one outlet calling Memphis 6-1 and ESPN ran a Windhorst and MacMahon piece on the staying power of Memphis. Preseason previews had tempered expectations after the Ja Morant and Jaren Jackson Jr. trades, so the fast start has been a pleasant surprise. I could not find specific subreddit threads, so fan mood beyond the media coverage is not confirmed.
outlook: Memphis visits New Orleans on Friday night in an NBA Cup group game as a 3.5 point favorite, and the Pelicans are 4-8 and allow 124.3 points a game. The model gives Memphis a 65.3% chance to win, so a bounce back is reasonable if the turnovers get cleaned up.
